intro.page_title: Roberto Vallado | Full-Stack Developer & Security Researcher | Intro
intro.tagline: Security-focused developer who wants to make the internet a harder place to break, one bug at a time.
intro.p0: I'm Roberto, a full-stack developer and security enthusiast based in Québec. My goal is simple: build better, safer software and help make the internet a less broken place. Over five years of building production applications in C# / .NET and Angular gave me the craft of shipping reliable code. But it was actively hunting real-world security vulnerabilities on Bugcrowd that changed how I see every system I touch. I genuinely love finding bugs: figuring out how and why they exist, writing clear reproducible reports, and watching teams fix them. I think about attack surfaces the way most developers think about features.
intro.p1: On the AI frontier, I'm actively building with agentic AI, designing and integrating LLM-powered workflows that automate repetitive tasks, surface insights, and help businesses move faster without burning out their teams. I believe the most impactful AI work right now happens at the intersection of solid engineering and practical business problems, and that's exactly where I want to be.
intro.p2: I also do freelance web development and SEO consulting for marketing professionals and small businesses in Mexico and Latin America. I help clients build fast, well-structured websites, get found on Google through on-page SEO, structured data and Core Web Vitals optimization, and set up analytics that actually tell them what's working. Being multilingual (English, French, Portuguese and Spanish) means I can work directly with clients across the Americas without losing anything in translation.
intro.p3: In my day job at SSM Innovation Centre, I've grown from a co-op developer into a team lead, taking on mentorship, architectural decisions, and project planning responsibilities alongside the hands-on coding. I've also taught Web Applications and Business Applications Development at Sault College, which sharpened my ability to explain complex things clearly and meet people where they are.
intro.p4: I'm currently completing an AEC in Secure Application Development at Cégep Limoilou, and working towards CompTIA Network+, not to become a network engineer, but because understanding the networking and infrastructure layer makes me a sharper developer and a better security researcher. Knowing how packets move, how DNS resolves, how TLS handshakes work: that context closes the gap between writing code and understanding what can go wrong underneath it. The goal has always been the same: build things that are hard to break, and help fix the internet along the way.
intro.p5: If you're building something meaningful (whether that's a product, a platform, or a growth strategy), I'd love to be part of it. I'm always open to the right opportunity, freelance engagement, or just a good conversation about tech, AI, or digital marketing.
